Rashi on Shevuot 11a:1:1.hebrew: דקדושת דמים - אין בה אלא קדושת דמים, שלקחה מתרומת הלשכה. אבל בכלי לא קדשה קדושת הגוף, דתקדש קדושת הגוף, דמכתשת שנשחקה בה לאו כלי שרת היא:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:1:1.english: For [it has] sanctity of value - It has only the sanctity of value, because [the priests] purchased it with funds from the Temple chamber's [collection of shekels]. But it was not sanctified through a vessel [so as to] become sanctified with inherent sanctity, for the mortar in which it was ground is not a service vessel:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:2:1.english: By one who immersed that day - if he touched it:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:1.hebrew: המנחות - שמועלין בהן משהוקדשו, הן מנחת יחיד:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:1.english: The meal-offerings - [that one is liable for misusing from when they are consecrated are] the meal-offering of an individual:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:2.hebrew: מועלין בהן משהוקדשו - דקדושת דמים בת מעילה היא:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:2.english: One is liable for misusing them from when they are consecrated - for sanctity of [monetary] value is subject to [the law of] me'ila [misuse of consecrated property]:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:3.hebrew: קדשו בכלי - הביא לעזרה ונתנה בכלי שרת:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:3.english: They were consecrated in a vessel - [The owner] brought [the meal-offering] to the Temple courtyard and placed it in a service vessel:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:4.hebrew: הוכשרה - נגמרה קדושתה ליפסל בטבול יום, וכל לשון הכשר לשון תיקון, שמתקנו ומזמינו לכך:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:3:4.english: Hukhsheru - Its sanctity was completed, [so that it can] be disqualified through [contact with] one who immersed that day. And every [use of the] term "hechsher" is an expression of preparation, [meaning] that one prepares it and readies it for this [purpose]:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:1.english: The handful - of the meal-offering of an individual:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:2.hebrew: והלבונה - הכוונה ללבונה של מנחת יחיד:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:2.english: And the frankincense - [This refers to the frankincense] of the meal-offering of an individual:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:3.hebrew: ומנחת כהנים - שהיא כליל, ואינה נקמצת:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:3.english: And the meal-offering of priests - which is burned entirely [on the altar] and from which a handful is not taken:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:4.hebrew: ומנחת כהן משוח - חביתי של כהן גדול היא שבכל יום, מחציתה בבוקר ומחציתה בערב:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:4.english: And the meal-offering of the anointed priest - [This is] the griddle-cake offering (ḥavitei) of the High Priest, [offered] every day, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:5.hebrew: ומנחת נסכים - הבאה עם הבהמה: שלשה עשרונים לפר, ושני עשרונים לאיל, ועשרון לכבש, והן כולן כליל:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:5:5.english: And the meal-offering of libations - that which is brought with the animal: three tenths [of an ephah of flour] for a bull, two tenths for a ram, and one tenth for a lamb; and all of them are burned entirely [on the altar]:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:6:1.hebrew: קדשו בכלי כו' - והך דפליג לה המשנה בתרתי בבי, הך והך דלעיל דהמנחות מועלין בהן כו', משום דבסיפא יש חילוק ביניהם במילי אחרניתא במסכת מעילה: דבההיא דלעיל לא קתני "וחייבין עליה משום פיגול ונותר וטמא" בקדושת כלי עד שיקרב הקומץ, ובהנך שכולן כליל, קתני בקדושת כלי דידהו "וחייבין עליהם משום נותר ומשום טמא". קתני מיהא קטורת, וקתני "קדשו בכלי", וע"כ מתניתין לעיל גבי קדושת מכתשת תנא "נפסלת בטבול יום", ולא תנא לינה, והכא תנא לינה, ש"מ קדושת כלי דהכא לאו מכתשת היא, אלא כלי שבשעת הקטרה, דומיא דקומץ ולבונה ושאר השנויים כאן עמה, אלמא מכתשת לא מקדשא ליה קדושת הגוף:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:6:1.english: "They were consecrated in a vessel," etc. - And this [mishna], which divides it into two parts, [namely] this one and the one above, [where it says] "one is liable for me'ilah for the meal-offerings," etc. — [it does so] because in the latter clause there is a difference between them in other matters in tractate Me'ilah: For in the one above, it does not teach "and one is liable for it for piggul, notar, and [eating while] impure" with regard to vessel-sanctity until the kemitza [handful] is offered; but in these [items], all of which are entirely burned, it teaches, with regard to their vessel-sanctity, "and one is liable for them for notar and for [eating while] impure." At any rate, it teaches incense, and it teaches "they were consecrated in a vessel," and necessarily [the following]: the mishna above, regarding the sanctity of the mortar, taught "it is disqualified by a tevul yom," and did not teach [disqualification through] lodging overnight, whereas here it teaches lodging overnight. We learn from this that the vessel-sanctity here is not [that of] the mortar, but a vessel at the time of burning, similar to the kemitza, the frankincense, and the other [items] taught here with it. Evidently, the mortar does not endow it with sanctity of the body [itself]:

Rashi on Shevuot 11a:7:1.hebrew: הואיל וצורתה - אינה משנה את מראיתה. הלכך, אע"ג דקדושת הגוף היא, לא מיפסלא בלינה. ומיהו משקדשה בכלי ליקרב, גזור בה רבנן פסול לינה, דלמא אתי לאכשורי בשאר המתקדשים בכלי:
Rashi on Shevuot 11a:7:1.english: Since its form - does not change its appearance. Therefore, even though it is [an item with] inherent sanctity, it is not disqualified by being left overnight. However, once it has been sanctified in a vessel to be offered, the Rabbis decreed the disqualification of being left overnight upon it, lest [people] come to permit [as valid] other items sanctified in a vessel [that were left overnight]:

Tosafot on Shevuot 11a:3:1.hebrew: וכי תימא דכל קדושת דמים נפסל בטבול יום - וא"ת: בלא נתינה למכתשת נמי תיפסל, דמעיקרא נמי קדושת דמים הוא? וי"ל דאפילו קדושת דמים לא פסלה בטבול יום אלא בנתינה למכתשת, וכתישה שראוי להקריב; אבל קודם כתישה לא:
Tosafot on Shevuot 11a:3:1.english: And if you would say that all [items with] sanctity of value are disqualified by one who immersed that day - And if you ask: Even without placing [the ingredients] in the mortar, let it also be disqualified, for from the outset it is also sanctity of value? And one can say that even sanctity of value does not disqualify through one who immersed that day except upon placing [them] in the mortar and pounding, [at which point] it is fit to be offered; but before pounding, no:

Tosafot on Shevuot 11a:3:2.hebrew: הוכשרו ליפסל בטבול יום - וא"ת, כי לא קדשו בכלי נמי ליפסל בטבול יום, מידי דהוה אחולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש דמיפסל בטבול יום, כדמוכח בסוף נדה (דף עא: ושם), דתנן: היושבת על דם טהור מערה מים לפסח, ודייקינן: מערה, אין; נוגעת, לא; דחולין שנעשו על טהרת קודש כקודש דמו. וי"ל דתנא דהכא סבר לאו כקודש דמו, והא דאמרו כחזרו לומר דהתם דהרי הוא כמגע טמא מת בקדשים ולא לחולין. א"נ הכא מיירי מדאורייתא, וה"ה דמקודם לכן מיפסלי מדרבנן. ואם תאמר, א"כ מאי פריך לעיל? נימא דקדושת דמים היא, והא דקתני נפסלת בטבול יום היינו מדרבנן, וכמשנה ראשונה דהתם דסברה דכקודש דמו! וי"ל דאי מטעם דכקודש דמו מיפסלא בטבול יום, א"כ אפילו לא נתנה במכתשת נמי, דכיון דמדרבנן מיפסלא, אפי' אינה ראויה להקרב נמי. או שמא קטרת לא מיפסלא משום חולין שנעשו על טהרת קדש, דלא שייך בה האי טעמא כיון דלאו בת אכילה היא; אבל לעיל קאמר שפיר "וכ"ת כל קדושת דמים מיפסלא בטבול יום", ולא קשה ליה "אפי' לא נתנה במכתשת נמי", דלא מפסלא קדושת דמים כל זמן שמחוסר מעשה בגופו, דהיינו כתישה. והשתא נמי ניחא מה שמקשה, דאמאי לא פריך מרישא דתנא לעיל מהך דהמנחות כו' דמייתי הכא, ובפ"ב דמעילה (דף ט.): שתי הלחם ולחם הפנים מועלין בהם משהוקדשו, קרמו בתנור הוכשרו ליפסל בטבול יום; קרמו, אין; לא קרמו, לא. ולפי מה שפרישית דקדושת דמים לא מיפסלא בטבול יום כל זמן שמחוסר מעשה בגופו, לא ה"מ למיפרך מרישא, דאפילו נתנוה בתנור אכתי מחוסר קרימה, וכשישחט עליהן הזבח אחר הקרימה שהיא אפייה:
Tosafot on Shevuot 11a:3:2.english: They became fit to be disqualified through one who immersed that day - And if you say: Even when they were not consecrated in a vessel, they should also be disqualified through one who immersed that day, just as in the case of unconsecrated food prepared in a state of Temple purity, which is disqualified through one who immersed that day, as is proven at the end of Niddah (71b, there), where we learned: A woman who sits [awaiting purification] on account of pure blood may pour water for the Passover offering; and we inferred: she may pour, yes; she may touch, no; for unconsecrated food prepared in a state of sanctity is like sacred food. And one can answer that the tanna here holds that it is not like sacred food, and as for what they said [there], it was as if they retracted, saying that there it is like contact with one impure from a corpse with regard to sacred items and not with regard to unconsecrated food. Alternatively, here [the Gemara] speaks of [disqualification] by Torah law, and it is equally true that earlier than that [point] they are disqualified by rabbinic law. And if you say: If so, what is [the Gemara] asking above? Let it say that it is sanctity of value, and that which it teaches that it is disqualified through one who immersed that day is by rabbinic law, in accordance with the first Mishnah there, which held that it is like sacred food! And one can answer that if it were disqualified through one who immersed that day on account of its being like sacred food, then even if it was not placed in the mortar it would also [be disqualified], for since it is disqualified by rabbinic law, [it would be so] even if it is not fit to be offered. Or perhaps incense is not disqualified on account of unconsecrated food prepared in a state of Temple purity, for that reason does not apply to it since it is not something that is eaten; but above [the Gemara] says properly, "And if you say that all sanctity of value is disqualified through one who immersed that day," and "even if it was not placed in the mortar" is not difficult for it, for sanctity of value does not disqualify as long as it still lacks an act done to its body, namely pounding. And now too it is well why [the Gemara] asks: Why does it not ask from the first clause that the tanna taught above, from this [mishna] of "the meal-offerings," etc., which it cites here, and in the second chapter of Me'ilah (9a): The two loaves and the showbread — one is liable for misusing them from when they are consecrated; once they have formed a crust in the oven, they become fit to be disqualified through one who immersed that day; if they formed a crust, yes; if they did not form a crust, no. And according to what I explained, that sanctity of value is not disqualified through one who immersed that day as long as it still lacks an act done to its body, it was not possible to ask from the first clause, for even if they placed it in the oven it still lacks the forming of a crust, and when the sacrifice is slaughtered over them after the crust forms, which is the baking:

Tosafot on Shevuot 11a:5:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה תיפסל בלינה אלמה תנן כו' - פירש בקונטרס דדייק מדקתני לעיל גבי מכתשת "טבול יום" ולא קתני "לינה", והכא תנא "לינה", ש"מ דכלי דהכא לאו מכתשת היא. אבל אי לאו הך מתניתין דמייתי, מברייתא גופה דמכתשת דקתני "טבול יום" ולא קתני "לינה", לא מצי למיפרך, דאיכא למימר תנא "טבול יום" וה"ה "לינה". וא"ת, ותקשה ליה מטבול יום גופיה: דבברייתא קתני דמכי נתנה למכתשת נפסלה בטבול יום, ואילו הכא תנן "קדשו בכלי הוכשרו ליפסל בטבול יום", דהיינו כלי דבשעת הקטרה; אין, לא קדשו, לא! וי"ל דהא לא הוה קשה ליה כולי האי, דמצי למימר דבקטרת אפילו לא קדשו בכלי נפסלת בטבול יום; והא דנקט "קדשו בכלי" לענין טבול יום, לא נקט אלא משום מנחת כהנים ומנחת כהן משוח השנויים כאן. [אבל לעיל דייק שפיר "לא קדשו לא" אטבול יום, דקדשו בכלי קאי אטבול יום ומחוסר כפורים ולינה, דאל"כ בחנם נקט ט"י.] תדע, דהא קומץ נמי אפילו לא קדש בכלי נפסל בטבול יום ובמחוסר כפורים ובלינה מכי נתקדשה המנחה בסיסא, כדקתני לעיל "המנחות מועלין בהן". והא דתנא קומץ בהדי הנך, משום סיפא דקתני "וחייבין משום נותר וטמא" דקאי אכולהו. אבל מלינה פריך שפיר, דליכא למימר דהוא הדין לא קדשו, ונקט "קדשו" משום מנחת כהנים וחביריה; דא"כ, אמאי תנא כלל קטורת בהדייהו? ועוד י"ל דהא פשיטא ליה דאין קטורת נפסלת בלינה משעת נתינה במכתשת, שהרי היו עושים אותה בתחלת השנה לצורך כל השנה, ולא מייתי מהך מתניתין אלא דשייך פסול לינה בקטורת, דאי לאו מתני' ה"א דאין שייך בקטורת פסול לינה כלל:
Tosafot on Shevuot 11a:5:1.english: "Rather, then, it should be disqualified through being left overnight. Why, then, did we learn..." etc. - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that [the Gemara] infers this from the fact that [the Baraita] above, regarding the mortar, taught "one who immersed that day" but did not teach "being left overnight," whereas here [the mishna] taught "being left overnight"; learn from this that the vessel here is not the mortar. But were it not for this mishna that [the Gemara] cites, [the Gemara] could not have objected from the Baraita itself about the mortar, which taught "one who immersed that day" but did not teach "being left overnight," for one could say that it taught "one who immersed that day" and the same applies to "being left overnight." And if you ask: [the Gemara] should also have difficulty from [the case of] one who immersed that day itself — for in the Baraita it taught that from when it was placed in the mortar it is disqualified by one who immersed that day, whereas here we learned, "Once they were consecrated in a vessel, they became fit to be disqualified through one who immersed that day," meaning a vessel at the time of the burning; [implying that] yes, [if] they were not consecrated, no! One can answer that [the Gemara] was not so troubled by this, for it could say that with incense, even if it was not consecrated in a vessel, it is disqualified by one who immersed that day; and that [the mishna] stated "consecrated in a vessel" with regard to one who immersed that day, it stated only because of the meal-offering of priests and the meal-offering of the anointed priest, which are taught here. [But above, [the Gemara] inferred properly "if they were not consecrated, no" regarding one who immersed that day, because "consecrated in a vessel" refers to one who immersed that day, and one lacking atonement, and being left overnight; for otherwise, [the mishna] mentioned one who immersed that day for nothing.] Know that this is so, for the handful too, even if it was not consecrated in a vessel, is disqualified by one who immersed that day, by one lacking atonement, and by being left overnight, from when the meal-offering was sanctified in the [priest's] vessel, as [the mishna] taught above, "one is liable for misusing the meal-offerings." And that [the mishna] taught the handful together with these others is because of the latter clause, which teaches "and they are liable for notar and for [eating while] impure," which refers to all of them. But regarding being left overnight, [the Gemara] objects properly, for one cannot say that the same applies [even] if they were not consecrated, and that [the mishna] stated "consecrated" because of the meal-offering of priests and its companions; for if so, why did it teach incense at all together with them? And furthermore, one can say that it was obvious to [the Gemara] that incense is not disqualified through being left overnight from the time of its placement in the mortar, since they would prepare it at the beginning of the year for the needs of the entire year; and [the Gemara] cites this mishna only to show that the disqualification of being left overnight does apply to incense, for were it not for the mishna, I would have thought that the disqualification of being left overnight does not apply to incense at all:
